beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: Hire three agents to search. Three more to decide. The filesystem is the meeting room.
beats.got: Six agents, and they share files. No idea what six agents cost.

beats.trigger: [Schedule your personal agent](exercises/personal-agent-homework.md) to read your challenge memory for a week.
beats.got: nothing new. It's homework, and I have no idea what it costs me or the company.

beats.trigger: **Analyze** handoff failures: hidden conflicts, clashing dialects, beige averaging
beats.got: nothing new. A list of verbs, with no figure and no payback anywhere.

beats.trigger: What do you expect will get lost between them?
beats.got: The question is fine, but it's about handoffs, not money.

beats.trigger: The agent writes the exact message first and sends only after approval.
beats.got: Approval before sending, and the scope is small enough to name. That's a control I'd accept in finance.

beats.trigger: Name the decision the crux blocks: the call you'd stay late to make.
beats.got: It names the one problem that blocks the rest. Useful, but I don't know if this is my material or the demo's.

beats.trigger: Three retrievers fetch raw material on your challenge into `sources/`; a fourth session curates it into `memory/` while they run.
beats.got: Four sessions at once for 28 minutes, and I have no idea what that costs in licences. I did the wiki one, since I have no connectors for the rest.

beats.trigger: You can't yet tell if it is right; that is expected.
beats.got: I paid 22 minutes for an answer nobody can check yet. That is exactly my problem with these programmes.

beats.trigger: Your team will ask: *when do I split, and how?*
beats.got: My team asks that, and I'd ask what it costs first.

beats.trigger: A mega-agent that does everything drifts in scope, and nobody can tell what it is responsible for.
beats.got: One agent per recurring workflow. That's the same logic as a cost centre.

beats.trigger: Default to one agent with a good prompt.
beats.got: The default is the cheap option and splitting has to justify itself. Finally something I agree with.

beats.trigger: A legal-policy agent shouldn't have customer-data access.
beats.got: There are three tests for splitting, and access is the one that matters for GDPR. Risk named before I raised it.

beats.trigger: Split for a reason, not because "three is more thorough"
beats.got: The module itself says more agents isn't more rigour. Fair, since the whole day was built on six.

beats.trigger: Three stances give you a spread of views, and a spread is not an answer.
beats.got: Without a framework the agent just averages. Fine, but it's still unchecked.

beats.trigger: Single-agent is the default; split only when one prompt cannot.
beats.got: A simple test to stop a vendor or my own team over-building.

beats.trigger: Pick this when the main session wants quick parallel thinking and a bounded return.
beats.got: nothing new. It's tool mechanics, and I'd leave this one to IT.

beats.trigger: Different tools: sessions; shared tools: helper agents.
beats.got: nothing new. I couldn't follow what 'tool surface' means.

beats.trigger: A retriever finds two numbers and the curator keeps one.
beats.got: The retrieval step can drop a number. In finance that's the failure I'd worry about most.

beats.trigger: A whole module showed multi-agent works. Don't apply it to everything.
beats.got: The module is honest that the exercise was a demo, not a recommendation. I respect that.

beats.trigger: Agents get stuck: wrong source, three views averaged into mush, the wrong file written, confident right before a failed handoff.
beats.got: A list of failure modes. The 'confident right before a failed handoff' one worries me.

beats.trigger: This prompt is long. Make your own variant.
beats.got: nothing new. I'm told to rewrite a long prompt myself, and I wouldn't.

beats.trigger: move the risky step from "do" to "propose."
beats.got: Check whether the bug is in the inputs, the processing or the boundary. 'Propose, don't do' is a control I'd use.

beats.trigger: Five minutes. The agent reviews the four agent prompts, the retrieval files, the synthesizer's briefing and the conversation, then rewrites the root instructions file in place and reports what changed.
beats.got: The agent rewrites its own rules file. Who approves that change?

beats.trigger: The audit reads how your agents handed work to each other; it does not check whether the briefing is true.
beats.got: The module admits nothing in the day checks whether the answer is correct. That's the first straight statement I've seen about it.

beats.trigger: Push back where it's wrong: *"The planner and the reframer needed to be separate."*
beats.got: nothing new. I'm supposed to argue with its summary, but I haven't got a basis to say it's wrong.

beats.trigger: Keep the unease about the synthesized briefing as an open question. Do not fix it today.
beats.got: I'm told to leave an open doubt in the briefing and go home. I'd never sign off a report like that.

beats.trigger: Skip if the memory still serves you.
beats.got: nothing new. It's optional homework and I'll skip it.

beats.trigger: Split only where agents can't be one: access, dialect, stance.
beats.got: Split only when access, dialect or stance differ. One sentence I could repeat.

beats.trigger: [Agent Trigger List, After Module 3]
beats.got: nothing new. More reading, none of it with a number in it.

beats.trigger: Agent risk sits on top of normal security.
beats.got: Agents add prompt injection and secrets in context on top of normal security. That's the risk talk I wanted at the start of the day.

beats.trigger: ## Bring to Module 4: what's the worst thing it could do with that access?
beats.got: Ask what the worst case is for each access. I'd ask the same of any system that touches finance data.

beats.trigger: You're close to an agent system that cracks your crux.
beats.got: nothing new. 'You're close' with no cost or payback is the promise I've heard from three digital programmes.

take_homes: Start with one agent and one good prompt. Split only when access, dialect or stance differ, and a vendor selling six agents has to pass that test.
The checking happens between the agents. Retrievers drop numbers and synthesizers average, so I'd want a human gate and 'propose, not do' on anything touching finance data.
The day never checked whether the final briefing is true, and it told me to hold the doubt. I'd treat all of the output as unverified.

monday.move: nothing on agents. I'd ask my controller what one month-end variance commentary costs in hours today, so there is a baseline to compare against.
monday.stop_condition: no pilot until IT has approved the tool for finance data and we have a per-user monthly cost
monday.blocker: IT hasn't approved the tool for finance data, and the module gave no cost or payback figure to put in front of the CEO

misconception.why: The module never said what any of this costs per person or per month, and it never showed a before-and-after number. 'Start with don't' helped a bit, but it still reads to me like buying a licence and hoping.

one_line: Honest about the risks and the 'don't split' rule, but I spent an afternoon on six agents and the day gave me no number I could take to the board.
